text: HTTPS is the first line of defense for any website, encrypting data between the user and the server so that hackers cannot read sensitive information. However, encryption alone is not enough. Authentication ensures that only authorized users can access private areas, usually through passwords or multi-factor verification. Next, input validation is critical—never trust what a user types into a form. Without it, attackers can inject malicious code or SQL commands, leading to common vulnerabilities like SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), and broken access controls. Regularly updating software and using security headers also reduce risks. In short, a secure website layers HTTPS, strong authentication, and strict input checks to protect both users and data.
